Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Zenith Insurance Group Q3 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Zenith Insurance Group's third quarter 2023 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Alex Harper, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Maria Gonzalez, Chief Underwriting Officer; Kevin Patel, Chief Investment Officer; and Dr. Elena Ruiz, Chief Claims Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we are making today may be considered forward-looking. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected. We encourage you to review our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties.

I will now turn the call over to Alex Harper.

Alex Harper: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on Zenith Insurance Group's performance for Q3. We delivered strong results, driven by net written premiums growth across key lines of business, robust new business production volumes, disciplined premium growth outlook, a favorable combined ratio trajectory, an effective reinsurance program, positive reserve development trends, and proactive share repurchase activity. We are making significant progress on our digital transformation initiatives, including enhancements to our ZenithOne platform that are boosting quote-to-issue conversions and operational efficiencies.

Jordan, our CFO, will now provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Jordan Lee: Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. As Alex mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Our net income was $520 million, or $2.12 per share. Key drivers of our financial performance included top-line expansion from net written premiums, new business momentum, underwriting discipline reflected in our combined ratio, reinsurance recoveries, reserve releases, and capital returns via buybacks. Our combined ratio was 92.8%. Investment income for the quarter was $310 million. We continue to maintain a strong capital position, with an RBC ratio of 560%. Our expense ratio also improved to 27.2%.

Let me dive deeper into our top-line performance, starting with net written premiums, or NWP, growth by line of business. NWP is a critical leading indicator for our underwriting portfolio health, calculated as gross written premiums less cessions to reinsurers. Excluding the impacts of foreign exchange and notable M&A—like our integration of the Midwest Commercial acquisition from last year—our consolidated NWP grew 9.2% year-over-year to $4.8 billion in Q3. This marks our ninth straight quarter of double-digit ex-FX growth, driven by disciplined pricing, strong retention above 90% across the board, and new business bookings up 15% from proactive digital distribution channels.

Breaking this down by our core lines of business, Property & Casualty, which represents 65% of our NWP mix, delivered 10.1% growth to $3.1 billion. Within P&C, personal lines were the standout performer at 12.5% growth, fueled by auto at +14.2% and homeowners at +10.8%. Personal auto NWP reached $1.2 billion, benefiting from our Snapshot telematics program—now adopted by over 3.5 million policyholders, akin to Progressive's model but with our proprietary AI-driven behavioral scoring. This initiative has improved rate adequacy by segmenting low-risk drivers, allowing us to file and win 8-10% average rate increases across 42 states amid persistent inflation in repair costs, which rose 7% YoY per Mitchell data. Bodily injury claims severity remains elevated due to social inflation, but our loss ratio held steady at 62%, thanks to enhanced fraud detection via machine learning, flagging 22% more suspicious claims quarter-over-quarter.

Homeowners grew to $850 million in NWP, up 10.8%, despite a benign CAT year so far—no major U.S. hurricanes impacting our book. We've leaned into bundled offerings with our HomeShield product, which bundles parametric coverage for secondary perils like wildfires, mirroring Chubb's high-net-worth strategies. Retention here hit 92.5%, supported by 6% rate hikes in California and Florida, where we're navigating regulatory scrutiny but maintaining portfolio discipline by non-renewing 5% of underperforming risks in wildfire-exposed zones. Regionally, U.S. personal lines drove 70% of this growth, with Europe adding +8% via our UK motor expansion post-Brexit rate normalization.

Shifting to commercial P&C, which grew a solid 7.3% to $1.05 billion in NWP. Middle-market workers' comp led at +9.1%, reaching $450 million, as employers face talent shortages driving payroll exposure growth—up 5.2% per NCCI estimates. Our ZenithWorks platform, a B2B digital marketplace launched last year, has onboarded 12,000 SMB clients, similar to Next Insurance's playbook, enabling instant quoting and 20% faster bind rates. General liability grew +6.8%, tempered by softening rates in some E&S classes amid a still-hardening market; we've captured 11% premium growth here through selective underwriting, targeting GL construction risks with drone-enabled risk assessments reducing loss picks by 15%. Challenges persist in commercial auto, flat at +1.2% due to supply chain delays inflating physical damage severities, but our expense ratio improved to 28.5% via vendor consolidation with CCC Intelligent Solutions.

Regionally for commercial, North America was +8.2%, while Asia-Pacific contributed +4.5%—our Shanghai JV with Ping An ramped to $120 million NWP, focusing on supply chain liability amid China's export rebound. Europe lagged at +3.1%, hit by German flood residuals from Q2, but reinsurance renewals at January 1 secured 20% cheaper protection via multi-year deals with Swiss Re and Munich Re, preserving margins.

Specialty lines were our fastest grower at +16.8% to $550 million NWP, underscoring our diversification strategy. Cyber insurance surged +22.4% to $210 million, capitalizing on the hardening cyber market post-CrowdStrike outage analogs—rates up 15-20% per Marsh reports, with our CyberGuard policy now covering ransomware payroll extensions, attracting 25% more Fortune 1000 accounts. Directors & Officers (D&O) grew +14.2%, buoyed by IPO revival and M&A upticks, while our marine cargo line added +12% amid Red Sea disruptions rerouting 15% of global trade volumes. We've invested $50 million in parametric triggers here, partnering with RMS for modeled event response, which paid out $18 million frictionlessly during recent Panama Canal droughts.

Finally, our Life & Annuity segment grew more modestly at +4.7% to $150 million NWP, reflecting a deliberate de-emphasis as we optimize for higher ROE segments. Term life ticked up +6.2% via direct-to-consumer channels, but universal life was flat amid rising interest rates pressuring crediting strategies. Health, at +3.1%, benefited from ACA exchange expansions but faces Medicare Advantage headwinds like UnitedHealth's pricing pressures.

Strategically, this NWP trajectory reflects three pillars: first, pricing discipline—aggregate earned rate of +7.8% across the book, per our Milliman audits; second, tech-led growth, with $200 million invested in our ZenithOne platform, boosting quote-to-issue conversions by 30% and mirroring Lemonade's AI efficiencies without the volatility; third, reinsurance optimization, where our 1/1 renewals reduced cessions by 2 points of GWP, improving the ceded ratio to 22%. Looking ahead, we guide full-year NWP growth of 8-10%, with Q4 acceleration from holiday auto bookings and cyber renewals. Risks include California wildfire season and potential Fed pauses inflating auto severities, but our attritional loss ratio target of 60% remains intact.

Building on this momentum, let's turn to new business production volume, a key leading indicator of our top-line growth and long-term embedded value creation. For the quarter, we delivered a standout performance, with new business annualized premium equivalent (APE) reaching $2.8 billion, up 18% year-over-year and 12% quarter-over-quarter. On a policy count basis, we wrote 1.45 million new policies, reflecting a 22% YoY increase and marking our strongest Q3 new business volume since 2019.

This robust production was broad-based across our core segments, driven by a favorable product mix shift toward higher-margin protection and savings products, enhanced digital distribution, and disciplined pricing amid moderating catastrophe losses. In our Property & Casualty Division, P&C new business APE hit $1.6 billion, up 21% YoY, fueled by strong demand in personal lines. Auto insurance led with 850,000 new policies at an average written premium of $1,450, benefiting from our telematics-powered "ZenithDrive" usage-based insurance program, which now penetrates 35% of new auto policies—up from 22% a year ago. Homeowners' new business grew 25% to $650 million APE, supported by rate adequacy in Florida and California markets post-2023 hurricane and wildfire seasons. We gained 120 basis points of market share in bundled auto/home, outpacing peers like Progressive and State Farm, thanks to our API integrations with mortgage lenders for embedded insurance at point-of-sale.

In Life & Health, APE reached $850 million, a 14% YoY increase, with 520,000 new policies. Term life dominated at 60% of volume, with case rates improving 15% to 2.8 policies per agent per day, driven by our revamped ZenithLife app, which uses AI-driven underwriting to deliver instant decisions on 75% of term applications under $1 million face value. Universal life and indexed products saw a mix shift, contributing 28% of volume versus 20% last year, reflecting advisor preferences amid higher interest rates. In group health, we added $150 million APE from mid-market renewals-as-new, capitalizing on ACA marketplace expansions.

Regionally, U.S. operations, our largest market at 65% of total new business, grew 20% YoY to $1.8 billion APE, with particular strength in the Southeast following rate filings averaging 9.2%—in line with industry trends from carriers like Travelers. Europe delivered 12% growth to $650 million APE, led by our UK motor book expansion via white-label partnerships with fintechs like Revolut, where we've embedded P&C products into 15% of their premium user base. Asia-Pacific was the star, surging 32% to $350 million APE, primarily from India and Indonesia life sales through bancassurance ties with HDFC Bank and Bank Mandiri. Challenges persisted in Japan due to yen volatility, but our variable annuity launches mitigated this with 18% volume growth there.

Underpinning this was a 25% YoY increase in digital submissions, now 58% of total new business, powered by our GenAI "UnderwriteAI" platform, which reduced manual intervention by 40% and improved persistency signals in real-time. We're also leveraging IoT data from 2.5 million connected devices in our P&C book to personalize pricing, yielding a 5-point improvement in conversion rates. Competitively, our value of new business margin expanded 220 basis points to 28%, outstripping Lemonade's digital-first model and Root's telematics focus, while maintaining profitability.

This production reflects our "Growth Accelerator" strategy: prioritizing high-VNB products (now 72% of mix, up from 65%), expanding distribution via 150+ embedded partnerships, and investing $250 million in 2024 capex for cloud-based policy admin systems. Amid softening commercial lines competition from Berkshire Hathaway subsidiaries, we're holding premium discipline, targeting 8-10% earned rate in the second half. Risks include potential rate compression if loss trends stabilize, but our APV sensitivity to a 50 bps rate hike positions us well. Looking forward, we guide to full-year 2024 new business APE of $10.5-11.0 billion, implying 16-19% growth, with Q4 seasonality favoring P&C.

Now, providing some color on our outlook for premium growth, which is a key driver of our top-line trajectory and embedded profitability. We measure premium growth primarily through net premiums written, or NPW, which captures both earned premium expansion and our disciplined underwriting approach. In Q3, we delivered NPW growth of 12.4% year-over-year, reaching $4.8 billion, ahead of our initial guide of 10-11%. This was fueled by a combination of rate, volume, and mix tailwinds. P&C lines—which make up 72% of our book—grew 14.2%, driven by mid-teens rate increases in commercial multi-peril and excess & surplus segments. Personal lines auto premiums expanded 9.8%, benefiting from our telematics-based usage pricing model.

For Q4 2023, we expect 10-12% year-over-year NPW growth, to $5.1 to $5.3 billion. Rate contribution: +7-8%, with commercial lines leading at 9-11% after successful renewals in workers' comp and D&O. Volume and new business: +3-4%, anchored by 15% growth in our specialty E&S division. U.S. operations, 65% of NPW, should grow 12-14%, buoyed by California wildfire repricing and Florida hurricane rate adequacy. Europe targets 8-10%, offset by strong German commercial expansion. Asia-Pacific rounds out at mid-teens growth in telematics auto partnerships and parametric products.

Key initiatives include our 'ZenithTech 2.0' platform, live across 85% of U.S. agencies, boosting quote conversion 22%. We're scaling embedded insurance via APIs with fintechs, targeting $300 million in attached premiums next year.

For full year 2024, premium growth guidance is 9-11% year-over-year NPW growth, to $21-22 billion. This implies a slight deceleration from 2023's 11.8% print, but still above our long-term 7-9% target. P&C at 10-12% growth, Life & Health at 6-8%. Strategic levers: $1.2 billion organic growth from digital, plus bolt-on M&A. Favorable retained accident year loss picks, but baking in $400-500 million cat load. Our combined ratio guidance remains 92-94% for 2024, supporting ROE expansion to 14-15%.

Turning to combined ratio performance, both overall and by segment, which remains the cornerstone of our underwriting discipline. For Q3, our overall P&C combined ratio came in at 92.8%, a 140 basis point improvement year-over-year, ex-cats at 89.9%. In the quarter, loss ratio improved to 66.4%, expense ratio at 26.7%.

Personal Lines delivered 94.2% full-year, with auto at 91.7% benefiting from ZenithDrive telematics, 11.5% rate increases. Commercial Lines at 91.8%, workers' comp and GL strong. Specialty & International at 93.9%, cyber at 89.2%.

These results reflect pricing discipline, portfolio optimization, and tech transformation—$250 million invested in GenAI claims triage. We guide to 92.5-94.5% for 2024.

Next, the effectiveness of our global reinsurance program. In Q3, gross written premiums reached $3.8 billion, up 8% YoY. We ceded $620 million—or 16.3% of GWP—maintaining 84% net retention. Gross incurred losses $1.2 billion, recoveries $720 million—a 60% rate—net losses $480 million, improving accident-year loss ratio to 58.2% net.

Our tower: $2.5 billion property cat cover to 1-in-250 year, high-layer XoL with Swiss Re, $300 million cat bond. Casualty quota share 25% with Berkshire and PartnerRe. Specialty ILW triggers.

North America: 65% recoveries on tornadoes. Europe: 70% on storms. Asia-Pacific: 55% on floods. This shaved 13 points off volatility.

On reserve development trends, we recorded net favorable reserve development of $185 million pretax, or 2.8 points to combined ratio. Year-to-date $520 million, 3.2 points. Strongest from 2021-2022 accident years, $120 million, personal auto 4.5 points.

By line: Personal $110 million favorable, commercial $60 million. Workers' comp $10 million unfavorable. Reserves $28.5 billion, 8.2% redundancy.

U.S. $140 million favorable, Europe $30 million. Tech like Reserving Excellence Platform improves accuracy 18%. Expect 2.5-3.0 points favorable annually.

Finally, share repurchase activity: In Q3, $650 million executed, YTD $2.3 billion, 2.1% of shares at $148.72 average. $10 billion authorization, $4.2 billion remaining. RBC 582%. Opportunistic at 12% discount to tangible book. Expect $800 million-$1.2 billion in Q4, enhancing ROE to 14-16%.

Maria Gonzalez: Thank you, Jordan. I'd like to provide an update on our underwriting performance. We've seen continued strong performance in our commercial P&C line. We are actively managing our exposure to catastrophe risks and have implemented several initiatives to improve our risk selection, including AI-driven underwriting models and drone assessments that are enhancing accuracy and reducing loss picks.

Kevin Patel: Thank you. From an investment perspective, we have continued to focus on diversifying our portfolio and managing risk in the current market environment. We are seeing positive returns from our investments in fixed income and alternatives, with our $45 billion portfolio yielding strong income amid higher rates.

Dr. Elena Ruiz: I'd like to briefly address our claims performance. We've implemented several initiatives to streamline our claims process and improve customer satisfaction, including GenAI triage and telehealth integrations. We are seeing positive results in terms of reduced claims processing times, down 25% in auto, and better fraud detection.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more color on the drivers behind your new business production volumes this quarter?

Alex Harper: Good morning, John. Absolutely. As Jordan detailed, our new business APE hit $2.8 billion, up 18% YoY, with 1.45 million policies. This was broad-based, led by P&C auto and homeowners via ZenithDrive and embedded partnerships. Digital submissions up 25%, UnderwriteAI reducing intervention by 40%. We're gaining share in bundled products and Southeast markets. This sets us up for sustained growth.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mary Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mary Lee: Good morning. Could you discuss the impact of inflation on your claims severity and reserve trends?

Jordan Lee: Good morning, Mary. Inflation remains elevated, particularly in auto repairs up 7% and medical trends, but our telematics and ML fraud detection have held loss ratios steady at 62% in personal auto. Reserve development was favorable $185 million, with personal lines releasing 3.5 points due to better severity outcomes. We're stress-testing for 4-6% social inflation, maintaining conservative Bornhuetter-Ferguson methods.

Operator: Our next question comes from Peter Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Peter Kim: What is the expected impact of reinsurance renewal pricing on your underwriting strategy going forward?

Maria Gonzalez: Good morning, Peter. Our January 1 renewals secured 20% cheaper protection via multi-year deals with Swiss Re and Munich Re, reducing cessions by 2 points. This enhances margins in Europe and Asia, allowing us to lean into growth in cyber and E&S while capping cat exposure at 1-in-250 year. Recoveries were 60% this quarter, stabilizing volatility.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen: Thanks. On combined ratio by segment, can you elaborate on the commercial lines strength and any segment-specific initiatives?

Jordan Lee: Hi Lisa. Commercial at 91.8%, driven by workers' comp and GL with 9.8% pricing and selective intake targeting 15% ROE. PYD 2.1 points from medical containment and virtual adjudication. Guidewire integrations automated 70% endorsements, expense to 28.6%. Outperforming peers through data center shifts.

Operator: Our final question today from David Wong with Citigroup. Please go ahead.

David Wong: Good morning. Thoughts on share repurchase pace and how it ties to your premium growth guidance?

Jordan Lee: Morning, David. Q3 repurchases $650 million, YTD $2.3 billion at discount to book. With RBC 582% and $3.5 billion FCF run-rate, we're deploying opportunistically under 10b5-1 plans. Ties directly to 9-11% 2024 NPW guide, as strong underwriting funds returns while investing in tech for margin expansion.

Alex Harper: Thank you for your questions and your interest in Zenith Insurance Group. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
